sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **The Great Escape**: Bose reached Japan via a German U-boat, arriving in Tokyo in **June 1943** to take command of the INA.
• **Transfer of Leadership**: **Rash Behari Bose**, the veteran revolutionary, handed over the leadership of the Indian Independence League (IIL) and the INA to Subhash Chandra Bose in **July 1943**.
• **Azad Hind Government**: Proclaimed in **Singapore (October 1943)**, with Bose as Head of State, Prime Minister, and Minister of War.
• **Key Metric**: The INA was the first military force to include a dedicated women's regiment, the **Rani of Jhansi Regiment**, led by Captain Lakshmi Sahgal.

items.definition: The political organization formed by Rash Behari Bose to mobilize Indians in Southeast Asia for the cause of Indian independence.
The diplomatic alliance Bose sought to leverage to secure military and financial support for the Indian liberation movement.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Delhi Chalo**: The famous slogan and call to action for the INA march towards the Indian border.
• **Imphal-Kohima Campaign**: The 1944 military offensive aimed at liberating Northeast India from British control.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Lack of air support, supply line disruptions, and the defeat of Japan in WWII.
• **Solutions**: The INA trials (1945) served as a catalyst for mass nationalist upsurge in India, forcing the British to realize their hold on the Indian military was slipping.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'S-A-I-L' (Singapore, Azad Hind, INA, Leadership).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Singapore (Proclamation), Azad Hind (Government), INA (Military), Leadership (Bose takes over from Rash Behari).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the formation of the INA (Mohan Singh) with the leadership of Subhash Chandra Bose. Always distinguish between the 'First INA' (1942) and the 'Second INA' (1943-45).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Transnational Nationalism' to describe Bose's strategy of using external geopolitical crises to achieve domestic sovereignty.

keyTakeaways: Bose's arrival in Japan transformed the INA from a small POW group into a potent political-military force.
The Azad Hind Government was a functional government-in-exile with its own currency, stamps, and civil code.
The INA trials post-WWII were the final nail in the coffin for British colonial rule in India.
